items.prompt: For the same 3-4-5 triangle, what is tan theta?
In the 3-4-5 triangle, angle theta has opposite side 3 and hypotenuse 5. What is sin theta?

items.answer: a / sin A = b / sin B, so 4 / sin 30 degrees = b / sin 60 degrees. Then b = (4 x sin 60 degrees) / sin 30 degrees = (4 x 0.8660) / 0.5, so b is about 6.93.
items.prompt: In triangle ABC, side a = 4 is opposite angle A = 30 degrees, and angle B = 60 degrees. Use the sine rule to find side b, showing your working.

items.answer: The sine rule links each side with the sine of its opposite angle, so it needs no right angle - a known side and its opposite angle form a complete pair that unlocks the other sides.
items.prompt: In one or two sentences: why does the sine rule work for a triangle with no right angle when SOH CAH TOA does not?

items.answer: The sine rule: a / sin A = b / sin B
choices: SOH CAH TOA on the whole triangle
The sine rule: a / sin A = b / sin B
items.prompt: A triangle has no right angle. Which rule finds an unknown side from a known side and two known angles?

items.answer: SOH: sin = opposite / hypotenuse. CAH: cos = adjacent / hypotenuse. TOA: tan = opposite / adjacent. So cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8.
